pending_qa.q: What are the key differences in packaging compliance requirements between European countries?
pending_qa.r: Regulations differ significantly country by country. In France, licensing is mandatory from the first kilogram of packaging with no quantity thresholds, includes a Triman logo labeling obligation, and requires a prevention plan since 2023. In Austria, there are also no quantity thresholds, but since 2023 it is mandatory to appoint an authorized representative if you do not have a branch in Austria.

pending_qa.q: What are the three main obligations for e-commerce merchants placing packaging on the German market?
pending_qa.r: The three packaging act obligations in Germany are: first, completing licensing (system participation) with a dual system via Licenseiro.de; second, registration in Lucid, the control authority registry under the packaging act, which provides you with a personal EPR Lucid number; and third, data reporting of packaging volumes both planned at year-end for the upcoming year and confirmed actual volumes after the year has passed.

pending_qa.q: What is the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) and what are its key environmental goals?
pending_qa.r: The PPWR is a proposed new regulation aiming to improve sustainability of packaging, reduce packaging waste, and harmonize regulations across EU member states while strengthening the circular economy and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Key milestones include requiring all packaging to be either reusable or recyclable by 2030, with specific requirements that packaging must be at least 70 percent recyclable by 2030 and at least 80 percent recyclable by 2038.

pending_qa.q: What is the timeline for PPWR implementation and when will it take effect?
pending_qa.r: The final approval of the definite version of the PPWR by the new European Parliament is planned for autumn 2024, and the regulations are set to take effect 18 months after the regulation comes into force, giving merchants time to prepare for compliance.

pending_qa.q: What standardized labeling requirements will the PPWR introduce for consumer packaging?
pending_qa.r: The PPWR introduces a standardized labeling regulation to simplify separation and make it easier for end consumers to dispose of packaging correctly. This uniform labeling aims to help consumers across different countries understand how to properly dispose of packaging regardless of where they are located.

pending_qa.q: What are the consequences for e-commerce merchants failing to comply with packaging regulations?
pending_qa.r: Consequences for non-compliance include fines, account suspensions if selling via marketplaces, and shipping restrictions. Additionally, control mechanisms will increase, as marketplaces and fulfillment providers will likely be required to check and verify that their merchants comply with all regulations, similar to what is already the case in Germany.

pending_qa.q: How much packaging waste was generated in the European Union and what does this represent per capita?
pending_qa.r: In 2022, the EU generated a total of 84 million tons of packaging waste, which corresponds to an average of 188 kilograms per person, demonstrating the significant scale of the packaging waste problem across Europe.

pending_qa.q: What other EPR schemes beyond packaging does InterZero help merchants comply with?
pending_qa.r: Beyond packaging, EPR requirements also apply differently from country to country to electronic devices (WEEE) and batteries. InterZero provides solutions for these schemes as well, and merchants can check their obligations regarding batteries and electric devices at epr.intelzero.de.

pending_qa.q: What is the Lucid number and why is it important for e-commerce merchants and fulfillment providers?
pending_qa.r: The Lucid number is a personal EPR registration number issued by the German control authority Lucid after a merchant completes their registration in the registry. Fulfillment providers and marketplaces require merchants to provide this Lucid number to sell or use their services, making it a critical compliance document.
